outcomes: Reads the n-m counts and the blue or orange tint of the control map on any square
Explains what the map adds (x-rays, pins, the exchange result, safe value) and what it still cannot see (sacrifices, tactics, king safety)
Glances at the map before moving, starting with the landing square
sources: app/src/lib/controlV2.ts (definition of the map v2, by the project)
Linked, not re-taught: L-SAF-COUNT-1, L-FND-COUNT-1, L-SAF-COUNT-FUTURE-1, L-POS-CENTER-CONTROL-1

steps.text: Under a lesson board, the **Control map** button paints every square at once. Each square shows two numbers, **White-Black**: how many White pieces and how many Black pieces attack it. **Blue** means White's number is higher, **orange** means Black's. Tap any square to see which pieces they are. Counting attackers is taught in its own lessons; here you learn to read the picture.

steps.caption: White to move. Turn on the map and tap f7.

line.say: The knight joins the bishop. The map on f7 changes from 1-1 to 2-1.

steps.text: The map does more than count. It adds **x-rays** (a rook behind a rook, a bishop behind its own pawn), skips a piece **pinned** to its king unless the capture stays on the pin line, and plays out the exchange with piece values to show who wins a capture there and each side's **safe value**. It still cannot see sacrifices, tactics, or king safety beyond that exchange. Read it as a strong hint, not a verdict.

steps.title: Same map, different truth
steps.prompt: Both boards have a black knight on e5 that looks at f3. Only one rook has moved. A plain count gives f3 as 0-1 in both. Can the knight really capture on f3? Predict first, then check. (The current map already knows about the pin.)

steps.text: Make the map a **habit before you move**, in this order. First, the square you want to land on: is Black's number above zero, and does the exchange favour Black? Second, your own pieces: any whose Black number is higher than yours? Third, look for what the map cannot see: a sacrifice, a fork, a threat to your king. Note that opening the map during a test or game counts as a hint.

steps.caption: White considers the knight jump to d4. What would the map say there?

line.say: On d4 the map would read 0-2: no White support, two Black attackers.
Black can take with the pawn.

steps.prompt: Which of the three map limits (pins, x-rays, a number is not a verdict) would you have forgotten in the last position? Name the square it would have misled you about, then rate your confidence (low / medium / high).
